lead: Four instruments answer four different questions. An energy meter counts how much energy a house has used, in kilowatt-hours. A megger checks whether insulation can still hold off a high voltage. A digital multimeter reads voltage, current or resistance at one point. A digital storage oscilloscope shows how a signal changes with time. An electrician, a wiring inspector and a final-year project team all need these tools, and each tool answers only its own question. Using the wrong one gives a number that looks correct and means nothing.
prereq: You need: Chapter 6.1 for how a coil produces deflection, and Unit 2 for RMS values and power factor.

blocks.text: Power tells you how fast energy is used. A bill needs the total, so the meter must add power over time. The induction energy meter, the drum-shaped meter on a wall, does this with a rotating aluminium disc.

Two coils drive the disc. The voltage coil, also called the pressure coil, is connected across the supply. It has many turns of thin wire, so its current is proportional to the supply voltage V. The current coil is in series with the load. It has a few turns of thick wire, so it carries the load current I. Both coils make alternating flux that cuts the disc and drives eddy currents inside it. Those eddy currents react with the flux and produce a torque proportional to V × I × cos φ, which is the power P.

A permanent brake magnet sits over the disc. Its field produces a drag that rises with disc speed. The disc speeds up until the drag equals the driving torque, so the steady speed is proportional to power. Speed proportional to power means the number of turns N is proportional to energy.
A worm gear drives the register, whose dials show kilowatt-hours. The meter constant K is the number of disc revolutions per kWh, typically 600 to 1200 for a domestic meter.

blocks.where: E is the energy in kWh (1 unit = 1 kWh); N is the number of disc revolutions; K is the meter constant in revolutions per kWh.

blocks.text: The megger measures insulation resistance. Insulation must hold off the working voltage, so a megger applies a high DC test voltage, commonly 500 V or 1000 V, from a hand-cranked generator or a battery-driven inverter. It shows resistance in MΩ. A common ohmmeter uses about 2 V, far too low to expose a weak spot that would break down at 230 V. Some syllabi call the megger an insulation resistance tester.

Isolate the circuit first, and disconnect loads and sensitive electronics. Connect the megger between live and earth, then between live and neutral. Never use a megger on a live circuit: the high voltage can shock a person and destroy the instrument. Discharge the circuit after the test, because cable capacitance holds charge. The scale runs from 0 to ∞ and is cramped near ∞. Many codes accept about 1 MΩ as the minimum for a 230 V installation; healthy new wiring reads several MΩ.

The digital multimeter (DMM) converts an analog quantity into a number with an ADC and shows it on a display. Voltage ranges have a high input impedance, typically 10 MΩ, so the meter draws almost no current and disturbs the circuit very little. Auto-ranging selects the range by itself. Continuity mode beeps when resistance is below a few tens of ohms. Diode test shows the forward drop, about 0.6 V for silicon. Current ranges have a very low resistance, so the meter must go in series with the load, never across the supply.
A DSO plots voltage against time. It shows shape, not just a number, so you can see distortion, spikes and timing.

items: The probe signal passes through an attenuator and amplifier, which scale it to suit the ADC.
The ADC samples the signal at the sample rate and writes the samples into memory.
The trigger decides when to record; a rising edge on a chosen level is the usual choice.
The time base sets seconds per division on the screen, and the memory holds the record so a single event can be studied.

blocks.text: The probe ground clip is connected to the oscilloscope chassis, which is earthed. It is not a floating input. Clipping that ground to a live wire shorts the live wire to earth through the probe. Use a differential probe or an isolation transformer when neither point is at earth potential. Keep the sample rate at least twice the highest signal frequency you want to see.

figure.caption: Two coils drive eddy currents in the aluminium disc; the brake magnet's drag sets the speed and the register gears count the revolutions as energy.

spec.title: Induction energy meter
spec.aria: Voltage and current coils drive an aluminium disc; a brake magnet controls its speed and a register counts the revolutions as energy.

examples.question: A single-phase energy meter with meter constant 1200 rev/kWh supplies a load at 230 V drawing 5 A at power factor 0.8 for 6 hours. Find (a) the power in W, (b) the energy in kWh, (c) the number of disc revolutions, (d) the cost at ₹8.00 per unit.
steps: Power P = V × I × cos φ = 230 × 5 × 0.8 = 920 W.
Energy E = P × t / 1000 = 920 × 6 / 1000 = 5.52 kWh. Since 1 unit = 1 kWh, this is 5.52 units.
examples.answer: The power is 920 W, the energy is 5.52 kWh, the disc makes 6624 revolutions and the bill is ₹44.16.
examples.check:
V = 230
I = 5
pf = 0.8
t = 6
K = 1200
rate = 8.0
P = V * I * pf
E = P * t / 1000
N = K * E
cost = E * rate
print(P)
print(E)
print(N)
print(cost)

traps: Energy is in kWh, not kW. 5.52 kWh is energy; 0.92 kW is power. Writing kWh as kW loses the whole idea of the meter.
A megger must never be used on a live circuit. The high DC test voltage is dangerous to the user and destroys the instrument.
A DSO ground clip is earthed, not a floating input. Clipping it to a live conductor short-circuits the supply through the probe.
A DMM in current mode has almost zero resistance. Connected across the supply instead of in series, it draws a huge current and blows its fuse.
The meter constant is in revolutions per kWh, not per kW. Rev/kW would describe speed, not energy.

quiz.q: State what the meter constant of an induction energy meter means and give its unit.
quiz.a: It is the number of revolutions of the disc per kilowatt-hour of energy, in revolutions per kWh.

quiz.q: What quantity does a megger measure, and what does it apply to the circuit?
quiz.a: It measures insulation resistance in MΩ, applying a high DC test voltage such as 500 V or 1000 V.

quiz.q: Why does the brake magnet make the disc speed proportional to power?
quiz.a: The magnet's eddy-current drag rises with speed. The disc settles where drag equals the driving torque, which is proportional to power, so speed is proportional to power.

quiz.q: Why can a DMM voltage reading be slightly wrong on a very high-resistance circuit?
quiz.a: The meter has a finite input impedance, typically 10 MΩ, so it draws a small current and loads the circuit, lowering the voltage it reads.

quiz.q: A meter of constant 600 rev/kWh makes 3000 revolutions. Find the energy recorded.
quiz.a: E = N / K = 3000 / 600 = 5 kWh, that is 5 units.

quiz.q: A student clips a DSO ground clip to the live wire of a 230 V socket to view the waveform. Explain what happens and what should be done instead.
quiz.a: The ground clip is connected to the earthed chassis, so it shorts live to earth through the probe: a large fault current flows and may damage the probe or trip the supply. Use a differential probe or an isolation transformer, or measure between two points that are both isolated from earth.

quiz.q: A megger shows 0.4 MΩ between live and earth on a domestic circuit. Is this acceptable, and what are the likely causes?
quiz.a: No. Many codes accept about 1 MΩ as the minimum for 230 V, and healthy wiring reads several MΩ. Dampness, damaged cable insulation or a faulty appliance are likely causes; each load should be isolated and the test repeated.

beyond: Not for the exam. Electricity boards are replacing electromechanical meters with smart meters that measure digitally and send readings over a communication link, so billing no longer needs a person to visit. Modern DSOs add protocol decoding, fast Fourier transform and deep memory for power-quality work. Clamp meters and current probes measure current without breaking the circuit. A useful search next is "smart meter AMI", "insulation resistance test IS 732" and "True RMS multimeter".
